news.title: Tensions rise over draft climate deal at COP31
news.summary: Bowen expects at least one more draft of the cover decision this week; Hoekstra says it needs significant change, and Saudi Arabia denies seeking to delay IPCC science.

news.title: 75 countries rally behind Türkiye's global electrification initiative at COP31
news.summary: Presidency figures show 75 countries and 94 organisations backing the 35x35 electrification goal, with the European Commission confirming EU support.

news.title: Timor-Leste calls for increased international financing for vulnerable nations at COP31
news.summary: As LDC Group chair, Timor-Leste seeks more loss and damage and adaptation finance and met Commissioner Hoekstra on finance, adaptation and loss and damage.

news.title: The EU has signed up to the COP31 global commitment on electrification: 35 per cent by 2035
news.summary: The EU endorses the presidency's 35x35 electrification pledge while Hoekstra and Darragh O'Brien stress implementing existing commitments over new rules.

news.title: COP31: Ambitious countries join forces
news.summary: Momentum builds outside the formal talks as countries still seeking ambition in Antalya spoke out together for the first time on Tuesday (paywalled).

news.title: Tensions rise over proposed deal at COP31
news.summary: European negotiators want a short, sharp cover decision; dozens of European, African and Pacific nations push for IPCC reports before the 2028 stocktake.

news.title: Spain allies with six other countries at COP31 to tax polluters and announces 45 million amid a struggle over the end of fossil fuels
news.summary: Seven countries including Spain and the UK back studying levies on polluting sectors; Spain pledges €45m for adaptation, loss and damage and early warning.

news.title: Tensions rise over COP31 draft deal
news.summary: Negotiators brace for tough talks on the 18-page draft cover decision; Hoekstra calls it a 'shopping list' as the IPCC timing row continues.

news.title: La UE exige cambios significativos en el borrador de la COP31 y rechaza reabrir los acuerdos de financiación
news.summary: The EU calls for significant changes to the COP31 draft cover text and refuses to reopen existing finance agreements.

news.title: COP31 Bulletin Day 8: Arab Group, Russia reject cover text over fossil fuels and electrification goal
news.summary: Ministers start refining the 18-page draft cover text; Arab Group and Russia reject it, LMDCs cite red lines, and the EU and Switzerland want no text on the finance work programme.

news.title: COP31 talks must drive a shift towards greener energy, EU climate chief says
news.summary: Hoekstra says the draft cover decision must keep the focus on sustained emission cuts; Bowen plans a revised draft later this week, with the deal due Friday.

news.title: COP31: Cover decision draft includes proposal for work programme on mountains and climate change
news.summary: Point 31 of the draft would set up a mountains work programme after a Nepal–Bhutan request; Nepal's negotiators say a finance and loss-and-damage ask is still under discussion.

news.title: COP31 draft urges 'accelerated action' on fossil fuels
news.summary: The draft calls for accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels and says tripled adaptation finance should reach at least $120bn; South Africa's David Maynier sets out ministers' priorities.

news.title: Chris Bowen launches bold climate agenda at COP31
news.summary: The 18-page draft, built on submissions from 160 countries, details 144 provisions; campaigners welcome strong fossil fuel language while 64 groups wrote to Bowen.

news.title: Pacific climate demands face resistance at COP31
news.summary: Bowen says 48 items are agreed and about 30 mandates remain; Pacific negotiators note the draft recognises the Pacific Resilience Facility but sets no funding target.

news.title: Coalition to move away from fossil fuels presses ahead without Colombia, its original champion
news.summary: Ireland and Tuvalu take over the Santa Marta coalition after Colombia's withdrawal; a progress report is due at COP31 and a second conference is planned for 2027.

news.title: COP31 enters decisive week as climate talks face political test and AI initiatives gather pace
news.summary: Ministers arrive for the high-level segment as Australia's first cover-decision draft divides parties; the Antalya AI Pledge reaches 80 endorsements and Solomon Islands pledges to the GCF.

news.title: Criticism of draft Cop31 deal text shows how tough climate negotiations will be
news.summary: The 18-page, 144-paragraph draft draws fire from campaigners, while Russia, the Arab Group and LMDCs dispute the need for a separate cover text. Friends of the Earth calls it "a mish-mash of contradictory proposals".

news.title: EU risks not securing any victories at COP31 if it refuses to engage on climate finance, according to several NGOs
news.summary: CAN Europe and Oxfam Germany warn that EU resistance on climate finance could cost it support on the fossil fuel roadmap and electrification; Hoekstra declined to discuss trade-offs.

news.title: COP31 draft calls for fossil fuel phaseout, at least $120bn in adaptation finance
news.summary: Reporting from Antalya: the draft seeks tripled adaptation finance of at least $120bn by 2035, with the Standing Committee on Finance setting a baseline for COP32, and Adaptation Fund and loss and damage pledges by end-2027.

news.title: Cop31 draft text is attempt to 'draw out parties' to find agreement, president of talks says
news.summary: Bowen defends the 144-item draft, which calls to immediately transition away from fossil fuels and limit 1.5°C overshoot; Russia, Saudi Arabia and the Arab group object to a cover decision.

news.title: First draft of COP31 deal signals tough negotiations to come
news.summary: Bowen says the 18-page draft holds clauses some nations already reject; it offers 'transitioning away' or 'phase out' fossil fuel options and flags divergent views on 35x35 and adaptation finance.

news.title: New COP31 Cover Decision draft - Oil Change International response
news.summary: OCI says the draft makes the right diagnosis but warns electrification must be renewables-led, not fossil gas or CCS, and that finance commitments lack accountability.

news.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'accelerated action' to exit fossil fuels
news.summary: The first draft cover decision urges accelerated action to phase out coal, oil and gas, voices deep concern over breaching 1.5C and calls for tripling adaptation finance to at least $120bn.

news.title: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
news.summary: Public climate finance pledged for developing countries has dropped by more than 70% in 2026; only five nations have new multi-year pledges, and Germany and France have yet to set out plans.

news.title: COP31 Bulletin Day 7: Sharp divisions lower expectations for COP outcome
news.summary: Emerging economies resist putting the electrification pledge and a fossil fuel roadmap in the cover decision; Germany's Heike Henn says neither needs anchoring there; a first draft is expected Monday.

news.title: COP31 turns to ministers for deal on finance, energy
news.summary: Bowen says a first overarching draft comes early this week but won't say if it mentions transitioning away from fossil fuels; the EU, Pacific islands and LDCs back the presidency's plan for the talks.

news.title: Climate Diplomacy Brief: COP31 day 7
news.summary: Previews the final week: ministerial pairs per negotiating stream, a revised cover text expected early in the week, and Hoekstra signalling the EU will not insist on absolute targets.

news.title: Africa stands united at COP31: Ministers demand delivery on climate finance, back AGN Chair
news.summary: Ghana's environment minister sets out Africa's demands on tripling adaptation finance and loss and damage; the AGN launches a pilot negotiation situation room.

news.title: COP31: What has been achieved so far?
news.summary: Charles Ellinas reviews the halfway point: methane commitments above $480 million, a health resilience initiative and the Commission's T-MED aim of up to €25 billion in Mediterranean investment by 2035; finance remains the main obstacle.

news.title: Africa battles EU 'delaying tactics' at COP31 over $120bn climate adaptation lifeline
news.summary: South Africa credits the African Group and BASIC for putting tripling of adaptation finance back into the draft cover decision after EU-led resistance.

news.title: EU blijft leidersrol spelen op COP, maar geen sprake van extra klimaatgeld voor arme landen, zegt eurocommissaris
news.summary: Before flying to Antalya, Hoekstra says expectations are low, backs the 35x35 electrification goal and rejects extra finance, citing over €32bn already paid out.

news.title: State of Play from Antalya: COP31 Midway Media Brief
news.summary: CAN says the EU, Japan and Norway objected to tripling-adaptation references, the EU proposed extending the mitigation work programme to 2040, and the just transition text offers only a website, annual meeting and reports.

news.title: 'Stop dicking around': Bowen facing uphill battle amidst insufficient progress at COP31 climate talks
news.summary: Greenpeace urges Bowen to strengthen, not dilute, cover-decision options in the presidency's summary of reflections, including the transition away from fossil fuels and a response to 1.5°C overshoot.

news.title: COP31 Finance Talks Stall as Developing Nations Seek Clear Rules on Wealthy Countries' Climate Funding Duties
news.summary: G77/China and LMDCs want a COP31 decision on the scope and timeline of the Article 9.1 finance work programme; the EU and other developed countries say Belém already settled it.

news.title: Africa battles EU 'delaying tactics' at COP31 over $120bn climate adaptation lifeline
news.summary: African and BASIC negotiators say the EU led efforts to keep tripling adaptation finance off the agenda; developed nations want it handled under climate finance rather than the adaptation goal.

news.title: Türkiye eyes ambitious climate outcome as COP31 enters final week
news.summary: Türkiye wants its 35%-by-2035 electrification goal in the cover decision, while the EU's call for 'clean' electrification may spark debate over fossil fuels' role.

news.title: COP31 president urges countries not to delay climate targets
news.summary: In a CNN interview, Murat Kurum urges states not to delay targets, backs clean 35-by-35 electrification and says fossil fuels will not be a significant future energy source.

news.title: Push for electric energy at COP31
news.summary: As COP31 enters its second week, Australia and Türkiye press for an electrification deal criticised for not requiring renewable power; Bowen expects a first draft text early next week.

news.title: Scientists defend UN overshoot report after Saudi-led push to sideline it at COP31
news.summary: Authors of UNEP's 'Limiting Overshoot' report defend its peer review after the Arab Group challenged it; the LMDCs want no references to non-UNFCCC reports, while the EU, UK, LDCs and AOSIS push to prioritise overshoot.

voices.name: Wopke Hoekstra
voices.role: EU Commissioner for Climate, Net Zero and Clean Growth
voices.latest: Calls the draft cover decision a distraction with many characteristics of a shopping list that reopens old issues, and says it needs significant change.

voices.name: Darragh O'Brien
voices.role: Irish Minister for Climate; head of the EU delegation
voices.latest: "COP31 must be the turning point where commitments become tangible reality."

voices.name: Murat Kurum
voices.latest: Says electrification is the answer, shielding communities from volatile markets while cutting emissions; pledges to turn past COP commitments into results.

voices.name: Chris Bowen
voices.role: COP31 President of Negotiations; Australian minister
voices.latest: Expects a first draft deal text early next week and wants to capture the ambition around electrification.

voices.name: Simon Stiell
voices.latest: Pledged UN support for Türkiye and Australia to make Antalya deliver for people, prosperity and planet.

voices.name: Samed Ağırbaş
voices.latest: Climate justice and finance top the agenda; success means delivering targets, not new announcements.

voices.name: Lynda Tabuya
voices.role: Fiji Minister for Climate Change; Pre-COP host
voices.latest: Set four Pacific priorities: 1.5°C, finance that reaches communities, ocean at the centre, Pacific leadership.

voices.name: Alden Meyer
voices.latest: On the deal: there has never been a shared COP presidency before.

position.headline: A mitigation package, not a headline target

points.v: Accepts 1.5°C is likely to be exceeded; backs an overshoot-peak-decline pathway to return below 1.5°C by 2100.
Effective implementation of national plans and urgent submission of missing NDCs.
Deliver the first global stocktake: transition away from fossil fuels and an accelerated clean energy transition, with clean electrification central.
Space in the talks for mitigation and a steer for the second global stocktake. Reuters reports the EU wants the mitigation work programme extended to 2040.
Mitigation and adaptation treated as complementary; resilience a prerequisite for prosperity.
Separate Council conclusions on climate finance adopted 9 Oct.
Stresses that all EU member states take part in COP31, a reference to Cyprus's exclusion from preparatory talks.

watch: Whether France's call for a more transactional line with emerging economies shapes EU tactics on the floor.
How the EU uses coalitions outside consensus talks, which Hoekstra has favoured.
Cyprus: Türkiye's handling of a member state the EU insists must participate.
The EU's proposed design for a Just Transition Mechanism, discussed by member states in September.

announcements.text: EU delegation head Diana Acconcia says the EU backs the electrification goal but insists it must come from clean energy sources.
Reuters: fossil producers and big consumers resist firm new targets; Turkey's electrification proposal doesn't require renewables, Brazil pushes transition roadmaps.
Russia's climate envoy tells Interfax it will table a statement against a 'hasty and forced' hydrocarbon phase-out and expects talks to overrun by a day or two.
Australia has reportedly confirmed it will not join the global methane pledge; agriculture talks look likely to be pushed to the June Bonn session.
Minister Darragh O'Brien travels to Antalya this weekend to co-lead EU negotiations with Wopke Hoekstra; Ireland plans to publish its fossil fuel transition roadmap on Monday.
Saturday: Simon Stiell press conference at 10:30 and a Presidency briefing at 13:00; negotiations pause on Sunday before the final week.
announcements.source: Climate Diplomacy Brief / The Irish Times

announcements.text: The leaders-level non-CO2 greenhouse gas summit drew over US$480 million in philanthropic pledges plus US$25 million for the CCAC's Super Pollutant accelerator.
Ahead of travelling to Antalya, Wopke Hoekstra signals readiness to compromise; Table.Briefings reports the EU will not insist on 'clean' electrification.
A draft text on the global goal on adaptation came out overnight; the African Group seeks tripled adaptation finance of at least $120bn a year by 2035.
An informal note on the new Just Transition Mechanism was issued late Friday; civil society groups criticised its limited scope.
The Mitigation Work Programme note is heavily bracketed; the EU wants it extended, with end-date options of 2030, 2031 or 2040.
A stocktaking plenary led by Türkiye and Australia is due Saturday night to show first red lines; a draft cover decision is expected early next week.
Arab states, Mexico, Korea and Switzerland have proposed moving to biennial COPs in co-presidency consultations on reforming the UN climate process.
Lula tells civil society in Antalya that Brazil should host the third conference on transitioning away from fossil fuels, likely in 2028.
Finland has published a domestic roadmap to phase out fossil fuels, following France, Germany and the Netherlands, though it sets no legally binding end date.
A civil society People's Climate Summit opened in Antalya with about 150 events through Wednesday, including a Monday focus on fossil fuel phase-out.
In cover-decision talks the Saudi-led Arab Group questioned the rigour of UNEP's overshoot report; the EU, UK, LDCs and small islands want COP31 to prioritise overshoot.
At his midpoint press conference, Simon Stiell urges parties to move swiftly to the hardest issues and avoid tactical delays, calling engagement 'constructive' so far.
Thousands marched in the rain through central Antalya demanding a fossil fuel exit and climate justice; police put the crowd above 7,000 and EFE reported no incidents.
UNFCCC confirms the Blue Zone will be closed on Sunday 15 November, with no meetings or accreditation; talks resume Monday 16 November.
COP31 President Murat Kurum tells CNN countries should not delay climate targets and calls 35% electrification by 2035 a key goal, provided the power is clean.
Developing countries accuse the EU of delaying tactics on tripling adaptation finance to $120bn a year; the goal was pushed back into the draft cover decision on Friday.
Technical loss and damage talks closed early Sunday without resolving core finance disputes; ministers take them up from Monday 16 November.
Bowen says talks span 160 agenda items and 60 substantive mandates, with ministerial and heads-of-delegation talks on the draft scheduled this week.
A 104-paragraph draft on the climate finance work programme offers end dates of COP32 or COP33; the EU, UK, Canada, Norway and Switzerland resist reopening its scope.
Hoekstra tells VRT NWS expectations for Antalya are low; the EU backs Türkiye's 35x35 electrification goal but will not promise extra climate finance.
Chris Bowen, presiding over the Antalya negotiations, expects a first draft deal text early next week and says the aim is to capture momentum on electrification.
CAN: loss and damage drafts include an option giving the Fund no guidance; the EU argues detailed guidance would interfere with the Board and says replenishment is already under way.
CAN: the G77 and China rejected Saturday's climate finance work programme text as too weak; a first draft cover decision is expected early this week.
Presidencies publish first draft cover decision: it calls for accelerated action to transition away from fossil fuels and tripling adaptation finance to at least $120bn.
350.org: the draft references 35% electrification by 2035 and welcomes Brazil's fossil fuel roadmap but sets no follow-up; it sees a backdoor for carbon removal.
Carbon Brief: new public climate finance pledges have dropped over 70% in 2026; Hoekstra said talk of new fresh money is 'dead in the water'.
The 18-page draft has 144 items, including a call to 'immediately transition away from fossil fuels' and to limit 1.5°C overshoot; more iterations are expected before Friday.
Negotiations president Chris Bowen called the draft a genuine attempt to see what parties can support, but declined to commit Australia to phasing out fossil fuel exports.
Daily Maverick reports the EU led efforts to keep tripling adaptation finance to $120bn a year off the agenda; African and BASIC pressure put it back into the draft cover decision.
Draft cover decision asks developed countries to pledge to the Adaptation Fund and loss and damage fund by end-2027 and proposes an 'Antalya-to-Addis Ababa roadmap'.
CAN Europe and Oxfam Germany accuse the EU of blocking progress on climate finance at COP31; Sweden and Finland lead the EU's finance negotiations this week.
The draft cover decision asks developed countries to reach net zero by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2040, and sets a 35% electricity share of energy by 2035.
350.org says the draft weakens fossil fuel commitments and that $120bn for adaptation falls far short of developing countries' needs; Greenpeace calls its language among the strongest yet.
Russia, the Arab Group and a China- and India-led bloc question the legal basis for a separate COP31 cover text; some want a simple presidency statement instead.
COP31 has a record 92,934 registrants, about 12,000 more than COP28, according to Carbon Brief figures cited by The Independent.
Bowen told reporters the EU has announced it will sign Türkiye's electrification pledge; the UK signed earlier.
African ministers (AMCEN) set five joint demands and three red lines for the high-level segment, centred on adaptation finance tracking and loss and damage.
Ministerial pairs for week two: Germany and India on mitigation, France and the Philippines on finance, Poland and Mexico on just transition, UK and Sierra Leone on adaptation.
Hoekstra says the EU will not push for absolute targets in the cover decision; in Saturday's plenary the EU pressed on 1.5°C overshoot and a stronger mitigation plan.
Türkiye's electrification pledge had about 30 signatories by Saturday; a revised cover-decision text from the co-presidency is expected Monday or Tuesday.
The EU, Pacific small island states and LDCs backed the presidency's proposed organisation of week-two talks; the Arab Group said it would not accept global targets imposed from above.
Arab Group and LMDCs reject new sectoral targets, incl. the 35x35 electrification pledge, in the cover decision; Saudi Arabia opposes referencing Brazil's fossil fuel roadmap.
German state secretary Heike Henn says neither Brazil's roadmap nor 35x35 needs anchoring in the cover decision; Germany backs the pledge and eyes the 2028 Global Stocktake for new goals.
A first draft of the cover decision is expected later Monday; the Turkish presidency plans to gather ministers mid-week to hear views on the text.
Canada will lend up to C$560m to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility over four years, taking pledges to about $8.2bn, still short of the $10bn target.
Oil Change International says a 35% electrification target only helps if it avoids locking in fossil gas, CCS and carbon removal; it wants progress on the just transition mechanism.
The draft offers two fossil fuel options: repeating 2023's 'transitioning away' wording or a stronger 'phase out'; Reuters notes both could be dropped from the final deal.
Chris Bowen says the 18-page draft contains clauses some nations have already rejected and the final text will not look exactly like it; the deal is due Friday.
Outside the negotiations, Türkiye launched an AI pledge; only nine of nearly 200 countries have signed so far.
UN News: ministers will meet in a 'Divan' this week to seek political compromises, with the formal high-level segment opening on Tuesday 17 November.
The Türkiye–ITU Antalya AI Pledge had 80 endorsements and 271 commitments by Monday morning; an Antalya Green Industrialization Compact was also launched.
Solomon Islands became the first country to announce a Green Climate Fund contribution at COP31.
Ireland and Tuvalu will take over leadership of the Santa Marta coalition on moving away from fossil fuels from Colombia and the Netherlands, after Colombia withdrew.
Bowen says negotiators have agreed 48 items, with around 30 mandates still needing outcomes; the draft text 'won't be the final draft'.
The loss and damage fund has 176 funding requests worth $2.8bn, with first approvals expected in December and replenishment from 2027.
Bowen says at least one more presidency-led draft of the cover decision is expected before the weekend, after ministerial consultations on sticking points.
The draft calls for 'accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels, including through the immediate transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems'.
The draft cover decision proposes a dedicated work programme and standing agenda item on mountains and climate change, following a joint Nepal–Bhutan submission.
Hoekstra tells delegates COP31 must send the 'strongest possible signal' on the clean energy transition, and urges a focus on sustained emission cuts.
Cardinal Pietro Parolin delivered a message from Pope Leo warning that the climate crisis is being overshadowed by geopolitical tensions.
At Monday's heads-of-delegation meeting, the Arab Group and Russia rejected the draft cover text outright; the LMDCs said it crosses red lines on 35x35, a fossil fuel roadmap and methane.
On the climate finance work programme, the EU and Switzerland called for no text, citing no new financial commitments; the poorest countries want a two-year extension and tripled adaptation finance.
Hoekstra warns the draft cover text could make the process 'untenable', telling reporters it has many characteristics of a shopping list.
Saudi Arabia defended its stance in the dispute over IPCC AR7 timing; AOSIS chair Ilana Seid called any delay unjustifiable.
European officials call the draft cover decision a 'Christmas wish list' and want a short, sharp text, calling some demands from a bloc including Saudi Arabia and India unacceptable.
Spain, the UK, Kenya, Timor-Leste, Vanuatu, South Sudan and Tuvalu signed a declaration calling for study of levies on polluting sectors to fund adaptation and loss and damage.
Spain's Sara Aagesen announced €45m: €25m for the Adaptation Fund, €15m for the loss and damage fund and €5m for a WMO observation programme.
The EU signed up to the COP31 presidency's '35x35' pledge to raise electricity to 35% of global final energy consumption by 2035.
Brazil's environment minister João Paulo Capobianco said deadlocks over the draft cover text could be overcome through adjustments in wording.
Chris Bowen says the cover text contains elements not all parties agree on and expects at least one more draft before the end of the week.
Saudi Arabia's delegation says it is not seeking to delay climate science, amid a dispute over publishing IPCC AR7 before COP33; the IPCC meets again in December.
The EU says the draft COP31 cover decision needs significant changes and rejects reopening previously agreed climate finance deals.
Per the COP31 presidency, 75 countries and 94 organisations now back the 35x35 electrification target, including Germany, the UK, Spain, Denmark and Japan.
Speaking for the LDC Group at presidency consultations on adaptation, Timor-Leste urged developed countries to raise adaptation finance to at least $120bn a year before 2035.
